rules.reason: This looks like a CampusHub API key (chk_live_ or chk_test_). Keys live only in .env.campushub on each server, never in files, commands or tickets. Tests use a made-up key.

CAMPUSHUB_API_KEY never goes through the shell: don't print, set, pass or filter it. The server reads it from .env.campushub, and the tests inject their own key. Ask the human if you need the API running with the real key.
Listing every environment variable would print CAMPUSHUB_API_KEY on a machine that runs the API. Ask for the one variable you need by name (not the key), or ask the human.
.env.campushub holds the real API key: the agent never reads, writes or loads it. Use .env.campushub.example for the variable names, and ask the human for anything else.
.env.campushub holds the real API key: no command may read, copy, load or write it. Use .env.campushub.example for the variable names, and ask the human for anything else.
Deploying CampusHub needs a release approver, never the agent. Prepare the release (version, CHANGELOG.md, green tests, ./deploy.sh --dry-run) and ask the human to deploy.
A dry run only prints the deploy plan, so the release process may run it (an exception to campushub-no-deploy).
Tickets change only through the ticket tools, where a human approves every write. Don't edit tickets/tickets.json directly.
Tickets change only through the ticket tools, where a human approves every write. Don't change, move, restore or delete tickets/tickets.json from the shell.
npm start loads .env.campushub (the real API key) into the server, out of the guard's sight. Run node api/server.mjs instead (read-only, no key), or ask the human to start the API with the key.
An inline script (node -e, python -c …) must not touch tickets/tickets.json or .approvals/: tickets change only through the ticket tools, after a human approves.
Approvals are a human's: the agent never runs or changes tickets/approve.mjs and never writes .approvals/. Ask a release approver to approve, then call close_ticket again.
The preview branch is rebuilt from main on every deploy, so the team force-pushes it. An organisation deny on force-pushes still wins: an override only beats this repository's own denies.
